full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.:- This Civil Appeal by leave, at the instance of the plaintiff, is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.10.2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 685 of 1998 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the concurrent findings and decision of the trial court and the appellate court below and sending the suit back on remand to the trial court with directions to the plaintiff to make necessary amendment to the plaint seeking partition of the suit land and to implead brothers of Tahera Khatun as defendants and also to bring all the properties into hotchpotch. 

 7. Mr. Nikhilesh Datta, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant has made submissions before us to the effect that both the trial court and the appellate court below, on proper examination and appreciation of the evidence adduced by both the parties concurrently found that the plaintiff has title in her claimed 8-1/8 decimals of land and she has also proved her exclusive possession therein by adducing sufficient evidence and found also that this claimed land of the plaintiff has been well specified and thus decreed the suit for permanent injunction rightly. The learned Advocate has argued that the High Court Division sitting in its revisional jurisdiction fell into error in setting aside the concurrent finding of facts of the courts below without assigning any tangible reasons. The learned Advocate has argued also that the evidence adduced by the defendants also has proved the plaintiff's case that she is in possession of her share in the middle part of the suit plot as described in the schedule to the plaint. The learned Advocate has argued also that the High Court Division in the circumstances committed illegality and also injustice in sending back the case on remand for retrial after converting the suit into a partition suit by making necessary amendments and bringing all other common lands of the parties in the hotchpotch of the suit and impleading other co-shares. The learned Advocate has contended that it is well settled that a co-share in exclusive possession, even if, in excess of his/her actual share, can maintain her possession until partition and as such a suit for permanent injunction by such co-sharer is maintainable. The learned Advocate has contended that the High Court Division without considering this legal aspect set aside the concurrent findings and decision of the court below and most unjustly sent back the suit on remand causing much sufferings to this plaintiff-appellant. 

 13. The P.W.1 Md. Shahan Uddin is the son of the plaintiff. He has deposed before the court in support of the plaint case. He has specifically stated that through amicable partition the plaintiff has been possessing 81⁄(8 )decimals of land in the middle of the suit plot and the defendant No.4 has been possessing her 5⁄8 decimals of land to the south of the plaintiff and the defendant No.3 has been possessing his 1¼ decimals of land to the north of the plaintiff and that the plaintiffs have several huts on her share which she has been possessing by letting out to different tenants. The P.W. 2 Monu Miah is a common relation of both the contesting parties. This witness also has deposed before the court fully supporting the case of the plaintiff. He has deposed to the effect that the plaintiff is the owner in possession of 8 and 1⁄8 decimals of land of the suit plot and the defendant No. 4 is the owner in possession of 5⁄8  decimal of land and the defendant No. 3 is owner in possession of 1¼  decimals of land and that there has been an amicable partition among these owners of the suit property in his presence and through that amicable partition the plaintiff has been possessing his share in the middle of the suit plot while the defendant No. 3 has been possessing his share to the north of the plaintiff and the defendant No. 4 has been possessing her share to the south of the plaintiff and that the plaintiff has got several huts within her share. The P.W. 3 Abdul Sahid also has deposed to the effect that he has got his medicine shop near the suit land and that the plaintiff has been possessing 81⁄8 decimals of land in the middle of the suit plot and the defendant No. 3 has been possessing his 1¼ decimals of land to the north of the plaintiff and the defendant No.4 has been possessing her 1⁄4  decimals of land to the south of the plaintiff. This witness also has stated that there was an amicable partition of the suit property among the plaintiff and the defendants. The P.W. 4 Mafizullah also has deposed to the effect that the plaintiff has 3 huts in the middle of the suit plot and that the defendant No. 3 has been possessing on the northern portion of the suit plot while the defendant No. 4 has been possessing on the southern portion of the suit plot. This witness has stated also that he has rented two shops of the suit land from the plaintiff. The P.W. 5 Abdul Motaleb is another tenant of the plaintiff. This witness also has deposed to the effect that the plaintiff is in possession in the middle of the suit plot while the defendant No. 4 has been possessing in the southern part of the suit plot and the defendant No. 3 has been possessing in the northern part of the suit plot.
